name: AXNav: Replaying Accessibility Tests from Natural Language
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). The abstract describes an accessibility testing workflow and a 10-participant user study.
summary: Introduces an LLM and pixel-based UI system that executes natural-language accessibility tests, records navigable videos and flags potential interface issues.

name: Computer User Interface Understanding. A New Dataset and a Learning Framework
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces desktop interaction videos and a framework combining synthetic examples with hierarchical contrastive learning for interface classification.

name: AgentStudio: A Toolkit for Building General Virtual Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: AgentStudio combines an interactive GUI/API environment with tools for creating tasks, annotating interface elements, and labeling actions in videos. Its online suite and GroundUI, IDMBench, and CriticBench datasets examine interaction, grounding, learning from video, and success detection.

name: VideoGUI: A Benchmark for GUI Automation from Instructional Videos
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Evaluates GUI automation from instructional videos at separate levels of high-level planning, action narration, and primitive execution.

name: GUI-World: A Video Benchmark and Dataset for Multimodal GUI-oriented Understanding
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces video-based GUI questions and annotations for studying temporal interface understanding across varied interaction settings.

name: WONDERBREAD: A Benchmark for Evaluating Multimodal Foundation Models on Business Process Management Tasks
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its normalized abstract SHA-256 matches the retained bibliographic snapshot. The demonstrations were rehearsed; their completion rate measures rehearsed human performance.
summary: Introduces WONDERBREAD, a benchmark pairing human WebArena workflow demonstrations with screen recordings, action logs, and written procedures. Six evaluation tasks cover documentation, knowledge transfer, and process improvement beyond end-to-end execution.

name: GUI Action Narrator: Where and When Did That Action Take Place?
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces Act2Cap and a cursor-guided method for describing GUI actions from video, with temporal and spatial localization challenges.

publication.identity_basis: Same work: normalized title, ordered author correspondence and the specific contribution in the complete publisher abstract were reviewed against the retained arXiv identity.

publication.title: VideoWebArena:  Evaluating Long Context Multimodal Agents with Video Understanding Web Tasks

name: VideoWebArena: Evaluating Long Context Multimodal Agents with Video Understanding Web Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Evaluates whether web agents can retain procedural skills and factual information from long video tutorials and use them during tasks.

name: UXAgent: An LLM Agent-Based Usability Testing Framework for Web Design
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). The system is intended to help researchers refine study designs before conducting studies with human participants.
summary: Introduces UXAgent, which uses simulated users and a browser connector to test website usability and present their actions, responses, and recordings to UX researchers.

name: Magma: A Foundation Model for Multimodal AI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). UI navigation is evaluated alongside robot manipulation and broader multimodal tasks.
summary: Introduces Magma, a multimodal agent model trained with labels for clickable GUI elements and video motion traces, and evaluated on UI navigation and robot tasks.

name: Mobile-Agent-V: A Video-Guided Approach for Effortless and Efficient Operational Knowledge Injection in Mobile Automation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. The authors identify arXiv:2505.13887 as an accidental duplicate and direct future updates to this record.
summary: Extracts operational guidance from video for mobile task execution and introduces Mobile-Knowledge to evaluate the contribution of external knowledge.

name: BEARCUBS: A benchmark for computer-using web agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: BEARCUBS provides 111 live-web information-seeking questions with short answers and human-validated browsing trajectories. Its tasks require multimodal computer interaction, including video understanding and navigation of interactive 3D content.

name: GUI-Xplore: Empowering Generalizable GUI Agents with One Exploration
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces GUI-Xplore exploration videos and downstream tasks, with an agent that combines action-aware modeling and graph-based environment reasoning.

name: TongUI: Internet-Scale Trajectories from Multimodal Web Tutorials for Generalized GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: TongUI converts multimodal online tutorials, including videos and articles, into GUI-agent trajectories. Its GUI-Net dataset contains 143,000 trajectories spanning five operating systems and more than 200 applications, and supports fine-tuning for grounding and navigation.

name: Scalable Video-to-Dataset Generation for Cross-Platform Mobile Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces MONDAY and an automated pipeline that extracts mobile-navigation training data from instructional videos across operating-system platforms.

name: VideoCAD: A Dataset and Model for Learning Long-Horizon 3D CAD UI Interactions from Video
notes: The contribution was reviewed from the retained abstract. Sections 1 and 3 of the exact-version v2 paper identify Onshape as the browser-based interaction environment with pixel-level input.
summary: Introduces synthetic CAD interaction videos, a model for learning interface actions from video, and evaluation tasks for spatial and long-horizon reasoning.

name: MM-BrowseComp: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Multimodal Browsing Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces MM-BrowseComp, a benchmark for browsing agents that must use evidence from web images and videos to answer multimodal search questions.

name: Watch and Learn: Learning to Use Computers from Online Videos
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). The reported agent evaluations use OSWorld and WindowsAgentArena.
summary: Introduces Watch & Learn (W&L), which converts human computer-use videos into UI action trajectories by predicting actions between consecutive screen states.

name: VideoAgentTrek: Computer Use Pretraining from Unlabeled Videos
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Extracts structured GUI actions from screen-recorded tutorials using inverse dynamics, then uses the inferred trajectories for computer-use training.

name: Learning from Online Videos at Inference Time for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: This work retrieves online video tutorials and converts them into structured GUI action demonstrations with short objectives. A two-stage selection process supplies a relevant local trajectory as in-context guidance at each execution step.

name: Video-Based Reward Modeling for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Builds ExeVR-53k from execution-video, instruction and reward triplets, including negative instructions with step annotations. A reward model uses spatiotemporal token pruning to judge task completion from the instruction and execution keyframes.

name: Ego2Web: A Web Agent Benchmark Grounded in Egocentric Videos
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Ego2Web pairs first-person videos with online tasks that require agents to connect the user’s physical context to web actions. It also evaluates an automatic task judge against human judgments and analyzes failures in video understanding and web execution.

name: CUA-Suite: Massive Human-annotated Video Demonstrations for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: CUA-Suite combines continuous expert desktop demonstrations in VideoCUA with the UI-Vision evaluation benchmark and GroundCUA grounding data. Screen recordings, cursor traces and layered annotations support study of temporal behavior and professional software workflows.

name: GUIDE: A Benchmark for Understanding and Assisting Users in Open-Ended GUI Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: GUIDE evaluates whether models can recognize a user’s behavior, infer intent and decide when to offer help during open-ended software tasks. It uses narrated screen recordings of novice users and studies the effect of additional user context on these assistance decisions.

name: GUIDE: Resolving Domain Bias in GUI Agents through Real-Time Web Video Retrieval and Plug-and-Play Annotation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: GUIDE retrieves relevant software tutorials through subtitle-based video search, then infers planning and grounding knowledge from consecutive annotated keyframes. It inserts that knowledge into existing GUI-agent modules without parameter updates and evaluates the plug-in on OSWorld.

name: MolmoPoint: Better Pointing for VLMs with Grounding Tokens
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Adjacent general VLM pointing method with an explicit GUI-grounding experiment; no autonomous GUI-task execution is established.
summary: MolmoPoint replaces textual coordinate generation with pointing tokens that select visual regions and refine them through subpatches. The general image/video method includes GUI-pointing evaluation on ScreenSpotPro alongside other visual grounding tasks.

name: Benchmarking and Improving GUI Agents in High-Dynamic Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces DynamicGUIBench for applications whose interfaces change between actions, together with DynamicUI, an agent that processes screen recordings. The agent selects informative frames, filters inconsistent action reasoning and uses trajectory reflection for subsequent decisions.

name: Beyond Screenshots: Evaluating VLMs' Understanding of UI Animations
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: AniMINT evaluates how VLMs perceive, explain and interpret UI animations using densely annotated videos. The study distinguishes basic motion recognition from higher-level animation meaning and probes motion, context and perceptual cues.

name: MMTB: Evaluating Terminal Agents on Multimedia-File Tasks
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Adjacent computer-automation benchmark using terminal workflows, explicitly separated from graphical-interface control.
summary: MultiMedia-TerminalBench evaluates agents that use terminal tools to work with audio and video files. The Terminus-MM harness adds multimedia perception to study how accessible evidence changes executable workflows and task outcomes.

publication.venue: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning

name: Video2GUI: Synthesizing Large-Scale Interaction Trajectories for Generalized GUI Agent Pretraining
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The abstract describes extracting trajectories from videos and reports downstream benchmark evaluations.
summary: Video2GUI extracts GUI interaction trajectories from tutorial videos to build WildGUI, a pretraining dataset spanning applications and websites.

name: OmniGUI: Benchmarking GUI Agents in Omni-Modal Smartphone Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: OmniGUI evaluates step-level action prediction from interleaved smartphone screenshots, synchronous audio and video. Expert demonstrations carry multimodal-dependency annotations, and initial baselines use native multimodal models as agent proxies to study temporal and audio-related failures.

name: Demo2Tutorial: From Human Experience to Multimodal Software Tutorials
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces Demo2Tutorial, which turns recorded software interactions into multimodal tutorials with task graphs and reports benefits for GUI-agent planning.

name: Benchmarking Living-Screen-Native GUI Agents on Short-Video Platforms
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: LivingScreen evaluates agents in a browser-based short-video environment where observing content consumes time and affects subsequent actions. Its task suite scores accuracy together with information efficiency to diagnose over- and under-observation on continuously changing screens.

name: Bridging VideoQA and Video-Guided Agentic Tasks via Generalized Keyframe Extraction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces VG-GUIBench to evaluate GUI agents following video tutorials, and TASKER to select task-relevant keyframes for video-guided tasks and VideoQA.

name: Agent-Computer Observation Interfaces Enable Dynamic Computer Use
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: The Agent-Computer Observation Interface separates continuous perception from discrete computer actions using captured frames, audio transcription and persistent visual narration. DynaCU-Bench tests these components on dynamic browser tasks and static controls, with model-specific ablations showing that additional observations can also hurt.

name: DigitalCoach: Communication and Grounding Gaps in Human and Agentic Computer Use Coaching
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: DigitalCoach records expert–novice software coaching conversations aligned with screen and input events. Automated and interactive evaluations examine how model coaches differ from humans in explanation, error diagnosis and visual grounding when helping a learner operate software.

name: GameWAM: A World Action Model for Video Games
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The main setting is video-game interaction, with GUI control included as an action mode.
summary: Introduces GameWAM, a model for native game play and GUI control that predicts future visuals and keyboard-mouse actions from synchronized gameplay and GUI trajectories.

name: Invisible in Space, Visible in Time: Motion Vision CAPTCHA against GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: MVCAP-Bench tests live browser CAPTCHAs whose foreground meaning emerges through motion against dynamic backgrounds. A foreground-only control separates temporal camouflage difficulty from answer format and browser interaction.

name: CUA-Master: Scaling Computer-use Agents through Open-World Recursive Improvements
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces CUA-Master, a computer-use training framework that mines workflows from instructional videos and turns them into synthesized tasks and trajectories.

name: AOI (Agent-Computer Observation Interface) & DynaCU-Bench
summary: AOI provides an adaptive video and audio perception layer for computer-use agents alongside the DynaCU-Bench dynamic GUI benchmark.

summary: Codex and Claude Agent Skill that drives live web products in a browser to record truth-linked walkthrough demo videos.

summary: CombatVLA is a vision-language-action model and action tracker for real-time combat control in 3D action role-playing PC games.

name: PSAI computer-use dataset
notes: Released by Paradigm Shift AI. The card reports 2,220 browser and 947 computer tasks over 294 websites and 173 applications, labels most tasks cross-platform with a few Windows or macOS tasks, and says human vendors performed the tasks under signed release agreements but that recordings may contain personal information. Hub API at revision 0e1b7c63: not gated, 16 parquet shards, 3,167 MP4 videos and 1,766 DOM-snapshot zips; there is no LICENSE file in the repository. The card metadata declares MIT for the data.
summary: Human computer-use recordings for 3,167 browser and desktop tasks, each with a screen video, input events and reasoning steps, plus screenshots or DOM snapshots for part of the tasks.

dataset_profile.notes: The OSWorld subset was selected post hoc using model outcomes; no train/test split is supplied. Coordinate calibration, task success, and complete anonymization are not established by package-format checks.

name: WorkDemo-350
notes: The card documents post hoc selection of the 286-task OSWorld subset based on model outcomes, uncalibrated coordinate annotations, and missing task-success acceptance records. It provides no train/test split or complete evaluator and does not claim complete anonymization. Review these limits before training or evaluation; the collection is an offline demonstration asset.
summary: Desktop demonstrations with task descriptions, videos, input logs, and action-linked screenshot evidence for studying reusable agent skills.

name: VideoAgentTrek-IDM-s1-7B
notes: Five safetensors shards of a Qwen2.5-VL checkpoint with tokenizer, processor and chat-template configs; the card declares Apache-2.0. The VideoAgentTrek video2action.py loads it through KEYFRAME_MODEL_PATH for stage 2 keyframe detection, with the IDM-s2 action identifier and an OpenAI-compatible API for validation and inner-monologue stages; a YOLO cursor detector filters videos beforehand.
summary: Keyframe detection model for the VideoAgentTrek Video2Action pipeline, the first inverse-dynamics stage that finds GUI interaction moments in screen-recorded tutorial videos before a second model labels the actions.

The author repository documents the action and video formats, and Section 3 of the v2 paper identifies the recorded Onshape browser interface. No archives or training samples were downloaded; operating-system coverage is unspecified.

name: VideoAgentTrek-IDM-s2-7B
notes: Five sharded safetensors files with processor and tokenizer configs; the card declares Apache-2.0. The README runs it after the VideoAgentTrek-ScreenFilter cursor detector and the VideoAgentTrek-IDM-s1-7B keyframe detector, and the pipeline also needs an OpenAI or DashScope API key.
summary: Action identification model in the VideoAgentTrek Video2Action pipeline, which recovers GUI actions such as clicks and typed text from screen-recorded tutorial videos to build computer-use training trajectories.

The card notes that a small fraction of annotated frames may be missing. The Video2GUI project README lists this repository as part of the WildGUI release. The data license is the card's CC-BY-NC-4.0 declaration; frames derived from third-party tutorial videos keep their own rights.

name: GuideBench
notes: Formerly published as saelyne/GuideBench; the Hub API redirects that name to this repository with the same object ID. Access is gated with automatic approval. The Hub manifest at revision 783caa86 holds three annotation JSON files (one per task), 40 task-description Markdown files, 120 think-aloud transcription JSON files and two CSV files under videos/; no video files are hosted in the repository. The project page lists Photoshop, GIMP, Figma, Canva, PowerPoint, Google Slides, Premiere Pro, CapCut, Google Sheets and Excel without naming operating systems; the environment facets follow from those applications. Models are evaluated on video snippets without the narrations. CC-BY-4.0 is the Hub data declaration.

name: VideoCUA
notes: At revision 6ecc530d raw_data/ holds one ZIP archive per application, 87 in total and about 26.1 GB. The card describes each archive as task folders with an action_log.json (instruction, platform and timestamped actions) and a 1920x1080 MP4 recording with its metadata; each action carries a groundcua_id that the card says identifies the matching annotated GroundCUA screenshot. Frame extraction into trajectories and LLM-written chain-of-thought steps come from a pipeline in the GroundCUA GitHub repository; this release holds raw recordings and logs as source material. The card names no operating system. The card's metadata declares MIT; its linked LICENSE file is absent from the repository. Task, hour and frame figures are publisher-reported.
summary: Expert desktop computer-use demonstrations from CUA-Suite: 30 fps screen recordings with millisecond-timestamped mouse and keyboard action logs for about 10K tasks in 87 applications.

name: WorldGUI-Bench
notes: The repository lists WorldGUI-data.zip and worldgui_metadata.json. The card declares an Apache-2.0 license.
summary: A desktop GUI evaluation dataset with user requests, instructional videos and pre-actions that vary task starting states. The release includes task metadata and a data archive.

name: VideoAgentTrek-ScreenFilter
notes: The repository holds one PyTorch checkpoint file, which video_preprocess.py loads as a YOLO model through YOLO_MODEL_PATH; license agpl-3.0 per the card. The README reports mining 39k YouTube tutorials into 1.52M interaction steps.
summary: Cursor-detection model in the VideoAgentTrek pipeline that filters screen-recorded tutorial videos by cursor presence before Video2Action extracts GUI action trajectories.

name: Magma-8B

name: WildGUI
notes: The card describes this as a personally reprocessed annotation release: records were regenerated and cleaned following the annotation workflow, then split so that each JSONL line holds one task with its ordered action trajectory; action parameters are omitted when grounding is unreliable (use_grounding false). The Video2GUI project README links this repository as the WildGUI dataset and names the joker-112/WildGUI_Screenshots repository as the host of the part16-part19 frames. Its figures of about 12M trajectories over more than 1,500 applications and websites describe WildGUI in the paper; the 19 JSONL shards (about 78 GB) were not downloaded, so the Hub record count is not established. The project README says trajectories and grounding boxes were produced by Gemini-3-Pro, so labels are model-generated. The data license is the card's CC-BY-NC-4.0 declaration; the source videos and screenshots keep their own rights, and the Apache-2.0 license of the project repository is not transferred to the data.
summary: WildGUI release from Video2GUI: per-task JSONL trajectories mined from Internet tutorial videos, with instructions, plans and grounded actions on web, desktop and mobile, plus screenshot shards for parts 1-15.

name: Computer Use Large (markov-ai)
notes: The card says the videos were sourced from the internet, trimmed to screen-recording segments and stripped of audio, and are meant for training and evaluating computer-use agents. Per-folder metadata.jsonl files give file name, category, trimmed duration and segment count only; there are no actions, cursor events or instructions. At Hub revision b50aecce the manifest lists 48,477 MP4 files, one fewer than the card (Excel has 8,110 against 8,111). The repository also holds descriptions.parquet and 48,473 per-video JSON files under descriptions/, beyond the card's documented files; the one inspected file gives the source video's title and channel, transcript text in 10-second windows and a short step description or NO_TASK per window. CC-BY-4.0 is the card's declaration for the videos.
summary: 48,478 trimmed, audio-free screen-recording videos (about 12,300 hours) of AutoCAD, Blender, Excel, Photoshop, Salesforce and VS Code use, gathered from the internet, with duration metadata and no action labels.

name: GUI-Xplore
notes: The paper's arXiv HTML links github.com/921112343/GUI-Xplore, whose README names this Hub dataset as the release; the paper link comes from the repository README. View-hierarchy files use Android uiautomator classes and Android package names, and the paper describes collection with DroidBot and crowd workers on cloud mobile devices. The card's summary line gives 32,569 QA pairs while its split table totals 35,316. The repository README lists the Xplore-Agent model, checkpoints and evaluation scripts as not yet released. Data license is CC-BY-4.0 per card metadata; it does not settle rights in third-party app content.
summary: Per-app Android exploration videos with screenshot and action sequences, view hierarchies and question-answer pairs for five tasks, from app overview and page analysis to action recall and sequence verification.
